```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7.5,
  fig.height = 4.6,
  dpi = 120

```

VaSSTra estimates states first and groups the state sequences second. The
`engine` decides how. A clustering engine (k-means, PAM, hierarchical)
assigns every observation to one state. A mixture-model engine, fitted with
the latents package, estimates how probable each state is for every
observation, so the uncertainty of a state is kept rather than discarded.
Two-level mixture models go one step further: they estimate the states and
the trajectory groups in one model.

| Engine | Indicators | Trajectories |
|---|---|---|
| `"lpa"` (default) | numeric, optionally with categorical ones | clustered from the state sequences |
| `"lca"` | categorical | clustered from the state sequences |
| `"multilpa"`, `"multilca"` | numeric / categorical | classes of subjects with their own mix of states |
| `"lta"` | numeric or categorical | classes of subjects with their own transitions |
| `"kmeans"`, `"pam"`, `"ward.D2"`, ... | numeric | clustered from the state sequences |

```{r library}
library(VaSStra)
data("engagement", package = "VaSStra")
```

## Latent profiles as states

The default engine is latent profile analysis. Each state is a profile with
its own mean on every indicator, and the engagement data's metadata names
the eight course-standardized indicators.

```{r lpa}
states <- states(engagement, n_states = 3,
                       labels = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"))
states
```

Every observation keeps its probability of each state. `uncertainty` is
what the most probable state leaves unexplained:

```{r posteriors}
head(as.data.frame(states, what = "posteriors"))
```

## Missing values without imputation

The engagement data carry 24 missing values from three singleton courses,
which the clustering engines fill with medians. A model engine can instead
use whatever each observation has (`missing = "fiml"`):

```{r fiml}
states(engagement, n_states = 3, missing = "fiml")
```

## States and trajectories in one model

With `"multilpa"`, students belong to classes that differ in how often they
are in each state. Those classes are the trajectories, estimated with the
states, so step 3 takes them from the model instead of clustering:

```{r multilpa}
by_mix <- vasstra(
  engagement,
  engine = "multilpa",
  n_states = 3,
  n_trajectories = 3,
  state_labels = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"),
  n_start = 10L
)
by_mix
as.data.frame(by_mix, unit = "trajectory")
```

`average_posterior` is how surely the model places the students of each
trajectory. The silhouette is reported on the Hamming distance as a
yardstick that can be compared with the clustering methods.

With `"lta"`, the classes differ in how students move between states:
each class has its own transition probabilities.

```{r lta}
by_movement <- vasstra(
  engagement,
  engine = "lta",
  n_states = 3,
  n_trajectories = 3,
  state_labels = c("Disengaged", "Average", "Active"),
  n_start = 10L
)
by_movement
```

`multilpa` is the special case of `lta` in which a student's state does not
depend on the previous one, so their BIC answers whether the order of
states matters here:

```{r order-matters}
fit_indices(by_mix)
fit_indices(by_movement)
```

The model without transitions has the lower BIC. These trajectories are
about which states the students occupy, not the order in which they pass
through them.

## Evaluating a model engine

A model engine's states are a latents model, so latents evaluates them.
`evaluate()` returns latents' comparison of other numbers of states and its
classification diagnostics of the fitted model, and draws latents' plots:

```{r evaluate}
evaluation <- evaluate(states, n_states = 2:5)
evaluation
```

```{r evaluate-plots, fig.height = 5}
plot(evaluation)
plot(evaluation, what = "diagnostics")
```

The criteria of the fitted model are latents' table as it is:

```{r fit-indices}
fit_indices(states)
```

## Categorical indicators

Latent class analysis takes categorical indicators. Here, three of the raw
counts are cut into thirds:

```{r lca}
levels_data <- within(engagement, {
  views <- cut(course_view_count, 3, labels = c("low", "mid", "high"))
  forum <- cut(forum_consume_count, 3, labels = c("low", "mid", "high"))
  days <- cut(active_days, 3, labels = c("low", "mid", "high"))
})
classes <- states(
  levels_data,
  variables = c("views", "forum", "days"),
  n_states = 3,
  engine = "lca"
)
head(summary(classes))
plot(classes, type = "bars")
```

## A model fitted with latents

A model fitted directly with latents can be handed over as it is. Its
states, and a two-level model's trajectory classes, are used as estimated;
`data` must be the data the model was fitted to.

```{r supplied}
indicators <- c(
  "course_view_count_z", "forum_consume_count_z", "forum_contribute_count_z",
  "lecture_view_count_z", "course_view_regularity_z", "session_count_z",
  "total_duration_z", "active_days_z"
)
model <- latents::multilpa(
  engagement, indicators, "user_id",
  n_profiles = 3, n_group_classes = 3, time = "sequence_position",
  model = "EEI", missing = "fiml", n_starts = 10, seed = 1
)
vasstra(engagement, engine = model)
```
